 Early voting ends in South Carolina after record turnout 
 Early voting ended Saturday in South Carolina, with voters across the state turning out in record numbers ahead of Tuesday’s midterm general election. By Kavya Ramesh Published : Oct. 31, 2026 at 7:15 PM EDT | Updated : 8 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google MOUNT PLEASANT, S.C. (WCSC) — Early voting ended Saturday in South Carolina, with voters across the state turning out in record numbers ahead of Tuesday’s midterm general election. 
 Voters streamed into Seacoast Church in Mount Pleasant throughout the day to avoid Tuesday’s lines. Saturday was the last chance to cast an early ballot. Early voting closed at 6 p.m. 
 Charleston County broke a record Friday, with more than 10,000 ballots cast in a single day. Over the two-week early voting period, more than 89,000 people voted early in the county. That total topped the county’s 2024 total by 20,000 ballots and was driven in part by voters under 44. South Carolina as a whole also saw record early voting turnout. 
 Saturday also fell on Halloween, and election workers welcomed voters who showed up in costume. 
 Many voters said skipping Tuesday’s lines was an easy decision. 
 “Tuesday is going to be madness. You don’t have to wait for your lunch line or, you know, your lunch break or anything like that,” Matthew Moore, a voter, said. 
 Moore said he voted early “so I don’t have to stand in line Tuesday, mainly. And vote my concerns.” 
 He said he also voted early a couple of years ago. 
 Eric Pettis, a voter, said work schedules were a factor in his decision. 
 “I mean, during the week, it’s busy when you work, and it’s a chance to cast your vote early, so you can avoid the crowds and just make sure it’s done,” Pettis said. 
 Pettis said he brought his daughter with him. 
 “On our way over here, I was explaining to my daughter that people have fought and died for this right to vote, so it’s very important to let our voices be heard for the people that are in charge over our country and our state,” Pettis said. 
 Emily Peoples, a voter, said she voted “because your vote matters.”
 Elizabeth McNaughton, a voter, said she appreciated that early voting was offered. 
 “Well, I think this election is important, and I really appreciate the early voting being an option for our community,” McNaughton said. 
 Voters who wait until Election Day can vote Tuesday from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Voters are reminded to bring a valid photo ID and verify their polling location before going to vote. 
 Absentee ballots must be returned to the county election office by 7 p.m. Tuesday.
